newsitem.title: USA: Power problems in Maine increase.
newsitem.headline: Power problems in Maine increase.

text.p: An estimated 47,000 Central Maine Power customers were without electricity Tuesday because of an ice storm, company officials said.
Fallen trees and branches had knocked out power to nearly 8 percent of CMP's customer base and some were unlikely to have service restored until midday Wednesday, spokesman Mark Ishkanian said.
"Just as soon as we restore power to one customer it seems like we lose power to two more," said Ishkanian. Augusta, Lewiston, Brunswick and the Sebago Lake region were among the areas hardest hit.
The National Weather Service issued winter storm warnings for western and central interior sections of Maine. Ishkanian said CMP has brought in extra repair crews from New Hampshire.
Bangor Hydro-Electric Co had "a couple of hundred" customers without power, spokesman Bill Cohen said.
